verdict.title: Unknown cause
verdict.explanation: The test is unreliable, but none of the tested conditions explains its failures. Possible causes: internal randomness, concurrency inside the test, or a factor FlakeLab did not test.

observations.label: Memory 128 MB
observations.text: Failed 10/10 runs with Memory 128 MB vs 0/10 at baseline (p < 0.001, significant after correction).

verdict.title: Memory sensitivity
verdict.explanation: The test fails more often when memory is limited. It may allocate more memory than a small CI runner provides.
verdict.fix: Use smaller test data, stream instead of loading everything into memory, or document the minimum runner memory.

reproduce.command: docker run --rm --network flakelab-net --memory 128m --memory-swap 128m flakelab-demo:latest python -m pytest tests/test_exports.py::test_export_catalog

verdict.title: Test-order dependency (shared state)
verdict.explanation: The test's result depends on which tests ran before it, so tests share state.
verdict.fix: Reset shared state in fixtures, avoid module-level mutable data, and make every test create the data it needs.

verdict.title: Resource sensitivity (CPU / timing)
verdict.explanation: The test fails more often when CPU is scarce. It probably depends on something finishing within a fixed time.
verdict.fix: Replace fixed sleeps and hard deadlines with condition-based waits, or mock the clock. If a deadline is a real requirement, test it separately on controlled hardware.

verdict.title: Environment assumption (timezone)
verdict.explanation: The test fails when the machine's timezone changes, so it assumes a particular local time.
verdict.fix: Use timezone-aware datetimes (UTC) in code, and pass time zones explicitly instead of relying on the machine's setting.

verdict.title: Hidden external dependency
verdict.explanation: The test fails more often without network access, so it depends on a service outside the test.
verdict.fix: Mock or fake the external service in unit tests, and move real network checks into a separate integration-test job.

clusters.interpretation: All members react to Network off and usually fail in the same runs: likely one shared dependency or event.
clusters.limitations: Tests are grouped by similar behaviour under the tested conditions. A shared signature suggests a shared kind of weakness; it does not prove a shared root cause. Signatures from few runs are noisy.

quality.note: Compares DNA clusters with the planted causes of the fixtures (1 = perfect agreement, 0 = chance level).
